title: Esau and Edom
lead: Esau, Jacob's older twin, became the father of Edom, the people of the red hill country south and east of the Dead Sea. Brother and rival to Israel through the whole Old Testament, Edom is judged by the prophets (Obadiah; Malachi 1:2–4), and in later Jewish tradition its name stood for Rome.

sections.b: The law commands, "Do not abhor an Edomite, for he is your brother" (Deuteronomy 23:7), and God gave Seir to Esau (Deuteronomy 2:5). Yet Edom refused Israel passage (Numbers 20:14–21), was conquered by David (2 Samuel 8:13–14), revolted (2 Kings 8:20–22), and joined in Jerusalem's fall (Psalm 137:7; Obadiah 10–14). Obadiah and Malachi announce its judgment. In Greek and Roman times Edomites lived in southern Judea (Idumea); Herod the Great was one. Herod's family, and later Rome itself, became "Edom" in rabbinic writings.
